model.acc_init: Eight accumulators initialised to XXH3_INIT_ACC = {PRIME32_3, PRIME64_1, PRIME64_2, PRIME64_3, PRIME64_4, PRIME32_2, PRIME64_5, PRIME32_1} from the .rodata constants at 0x455960/0x455950/0x453a30/0x4525e0. acc[5] is 0x85EBCA77 (PRIME32_2); an early draft misread the bytes at 0x453a30+8 as 0x27D4EB2F (PRIME32_4) and every hash was wrong -- corrected before submission, see the README
model.blocks: nbBlocks = (len-1) >> 10 full blocks of 16 stripes (1024 bytes). Each stripe is one accumulate_512 over 64 input bytes against a 64-byte secret window sliding 8 bytes per stripe (secret + s*8, restarting at the default secret each block). After each block, scrambleAcc with the secret + 128 window (acc[i] = (acc[i] ^ (acc[i] >> 47) ^ secret[i]) * 0x9E3779B1; the four .rodata constants are byte-identical to kSecret[128:192])
model.custom_secret: withSeed with seed != 0 builds a 192-byte custom secret on the stack at rsp+0x50: word 2i is kSecret[2i] + seed, word 2i+1 is kSecret[2i+1] - seed (the twelve 16-byte .rodata constants at 0x454530/0x455670/0x451170/0x452fc0/0x455fa0/0x450af0/0x4517e0/0x454540/0x454220/0x451ad0/0x451150/0x455970 are byte-identical to the twelve kSecret chunks), then runs the identical loop against that secret. The merge immediates in the seed != 0 path are loaded from the stack secret, not folded as constants
model.last_stripe: Always runs: accumulate_512 over input[len-64..len) against secret + 121 (the four .rodata constants 0x450ae0/0x4562d0/0x454520/0x451160 are byte-identical to kSecret[121:185])
model.merge: low64 = mergeAccs(acc, secret + 11, len * PRIME64_1); high64 = mergeAccs(acc, secret + 117, ~(len * PRIME64_2)). mergeAccs folds four 128-bit products (acc[2i] ^ secret[16i]) * (acc[2i+1] ^ secret[16i+8]) low ^ high, then XXH3_avalanche. All sixteen merge-window words appear as movabs immediates in the default body and in the withSeed seed==0 path: low window kSecret + 11, 19, 27, 35, 43, 51, 59, 67; high window kSecret + 117, 125, 133, 141, 149, 157, 165, 173
model.remaining_stripes: ((len-1) & 0x3ff) >> 6 stripes from the block boundary, secret restarting at kSecret + 0

return_value: 128-bit hash as (low64, high64) in (%rax, %rdx). The Hash2x64 wrappers store high64 through their first out-pointer argument and low64 through the second

semantics.scope: Lengths > 240 only, the hashLong helpers at 0x61d8a60 and 0x61d9bc0. Lengths 0..128 are reconstructed in PR #5578 and 129..240 in PR #5595; the 64-bit hashLong pair (0x61d8510/0x61d9090) and the 64-bit len_129to240 variant at 0x61d7dc0 are delegation targets / siblings only and are out of scope here
semantics.seed_term: The seed is folded only into the custom secret (word 2i += seed, word 2i+1 -= seed); with seed 0 the withSeed helper is exactly the default helper. The merge starts use len * PRIME64_1 and ~(len * PRIME64_2) with no seed term

side_effects: The default helper writes no memory, calls nothing except the stack-canary failure stub, and reads only [data, data+len) and the secret windows listed in the model. The withSeed helper additionally writes its 192-byte custom secret to its own stack frame. Both restore all callee-saved registers

tests.cases: 2,400 deterministic cases (1,200 per entry point; lengths 241..2048 cycled; 12 seeds including 0, 1, 2, PRIME64_1 and 0xffffffffffffffff). Transliteration vs independent loop-form reference: 0 mismatches. See result.json
tests.native_execution_check: During development the transliteration was checked by executing the extracted function bytes natively (a small C harness mapping the code and .rodata pages at the binary's own VAs, leaf functions, controlled input buffers): 120 random cases across both entry points, lengths 241..4096, 0 mismatches. A first Python/ctypes harness attempt segfaulted before any case because 0x450000 overlaps the interpreter's own mapping; moving the harness to a -no-pie C binary fixed the harness only. The committed cross-check is the Python reference, and the native execution is not an input to the generator
tests.oracle_check: The extracted bytes agree with the system libxxhash 0.8.2 oracle at the 128-bit entry points (XXH3_128bits / _withSeed, lengths 241..5000, 7 seeds): 0/600 mismatches; the oracle is not an input to the generator
tests.published_anchors: No published test vector exists for these helpers in isolation; the check values in check-values.tsv are computed values confirmed against the system oracle at the entry points
tests.unit_tests: tests/test_xxh3_hashlong_128b115.py, 11 tests (check values, out-of-scope rejection, transliteration-vs-reference agreement over all boundary lengths, seed sensitivity, seed-0 equivalence, secret-window sensitivity, custom-secret construction, binary grounding including the caller bodies, result regeneration)

unknowns: Whether any caller other than the two 128-bit entry points reaches these helpers is not established beyond the whole-.text E8/lea scan (exactly two call sites, no lea references)
The 64-bit hashLong pair at 0x61d8510/0x61d9090 and the 64-bit len_129to240 variant at 0x61d7dc0 are delegation targets / siblings only; their bodies are not reconstructed here

No source-level rationale is claimed for the withSeed custom-secret construction beyond the observed word-wise +/- seed pattern, or for the merge windows starting at secret+11 and secret+117; both are recorded as observed in the disassembly
